clips.label: Question 1
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Two-Part Scope of Work Structure. An integration contract separates the scope of work into deliverable scope and project scope. What distinction separates these two scope components? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Deliverable scope lists contractor hardware submittals, while project scope specifies owner preventive maintenance agreements. Option B. Deliverable scope details architectural drawing packages, while project scope outlines DSP programming and network commissioning. Option C. Deliverable scope establishes site safety protocols, while project scope defines system performance verification testing criteria. Option D. Deliverable scope defines product features, while project scope defines required execution work.

clips.label: Question 1, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Deliverable scope lists contractor hardware submittals, while project scope specifies owner preventive maintenance agreements. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "Deliverable scope lists contractor hardware…agreements" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Decisive rule: A complete scope of work includes both the deliverable scope (the features and functions of the product, process, or service delivered) and the project scope (the work that must be accomplished to deliver it), along with explicit in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries. Best answer: Deliverable scope defines product features, while project scope defines required execution work.

clips.label: Question 2
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Work Breakdown Structure Noun Convention. How are elements formatted in a Work Breakdown Structure compared to activities in a Logic Network Diagram? Choose the single best answer. Option A. WBS elements use verb phrases with calendar deadlines, whereas Logic Network elements use cost accounting codes. Option B. WBS elements show room elevation details, whereas Logic Network activities list conduit fill percentages and wire pulls. Option C. WBS elements identify technician labor classifications, whereas Logic Network activities show hourly billing rates and expenses. Option D. WBS elements are stated as nouns representing deliverables, whereas Logic Network activities are stated as verbs connected by dependencies.

clips.label: Question 2, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. WBS elements use verb phrases with calendar deadlines, whereas Logic Network elements use cost accounting codes. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "WBS elements use verb phrases with calendar…cost accounting codes" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Decisive rule: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) decomposes project deliverables into nouns without specifying who, when, or how much, whereas a Logic Network Diagram sequences activities written as verbs according to predecessor and successor dependencies. Best answer: WBS elements are stated as nouns representing deliverables, whereas Logic Network activities are stated as verbs connected by dependencies.

clips.label: Question 3
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Effort versus Duration Scheduling. Why does scheduling an AV installation using effort rather than duration frequently cause project delays? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Effort doubles technician headcount allocations across concurrent project tasks. Option B. Duration omits multi-project resource contention and travel time calculations. Option C. Effort calculations require substantial completion sign-off from the general contractor before scheduling starts. Option D. Effort measures labor hours without factoring calendar delays, travel, or competing demands.

clips.label: Interaction rationale 28
clips.text: Work from the governing relationship or dependency, not from memory alone. What should the installer do? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Fasten the screen housing and permit fabric to cover the fire alarm station. Option B. Detach the fire alarm station and recess it inside the wall cavity space. Option C. Cut an inspection viewing window directly into the projection screen fabric surface. Option D. Stop work and submit an RFI to resolve the life-safety clearance conflict.

clips.label: Question 84
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Passive PAD Insertion for Line-Level Overload. Mixer output voltage overloads a downstream processor fixed input stage during gain calibration. What modification resolves this overload? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Insert a passive resistive attenuator pad ahead of the processor input. Option B. Disconnect the AC safety earth ground terminal on the processor power supply. Option C. Short balanced audio input pins 2 and 3 together inside the XLR connector. Option D. Set downstream power amplifier input sensitivity potentiometers to maximum gain.

clips.label: Question 85
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Correcting VPN MTU Packet Fragmentation on Video Streams. Video streams stutter over an encrypted VPN due to packet fragmentation exceeding 1518 bytes. What configuration modification resolves this issue? Choose the best destination for the match. Option A. Replace horizontal Category 6A patch cords with voice-grade Category 3 unshielded wiring. Option B. Reduce video endpoint MTU size so VPN encapsulation headers do not exceed 1518 bytes. Option C. Configure room cameras to switch from progressive scanning to interlaced scanning modes. Option D. Reassign codec network interfaces to link-local automatic private IP addressing schemes.

clips.label: Question 85, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Replace horizontal Category 6A patch cords with voice-grade Category 3 unshielded wiring. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "Replace horizontal Category 6A patch cords…3 unshielded wiring" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Decisive rule: VPN encryption encapsulates packets in an extra header; if the resulting frame exceeds the 1518-byte Ethernet MTU limit, routers fragment each packet into two frames, ruining real-time media timing. Lowering the endpoint MTU prevents fragmentation. Best answer: Reduce video endpoint MTU size so VPN encapsulation headers do not exceed 1518 bytes.

clips.label: Question 90
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Ceiling Projector Substructure and Pipe Rigging Sequence. Arrange the steps for installing an overhead ceiling-mounted projector substructure and suspension pipe in the correct chronological sequence. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Verify structural engineer approval, confirm the 5:1 safety factor for combined device and hardware weight, and hand-check ceiling beams for HVAC vibration. Step 2: Anchor the adjustable steel-channel strut (Unistrut) bridge to primary building structure and attach the upper pipe flange. Step 3: Drop a plumb bob from the pipe flange to mark the ceiling tile, remove the tile to hole-saw the opening cleanly, and reinstall the tile. Step 4: Thread the continuous black-iron suspension pipe into the flange, lock all setscrews/safety bolts into the pipe threads, and attach the projector bracket.

clips.label: Question 105
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: No Cable Left Behind 4-Step Cable Pulling and Labeling Workflow. Order the four steps of the 'No Cable Left Behind' temporary cable labeling and pulling workflow in the exact sequence performed in the field. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Apply a matching temporary ID label ~600 mm (2 ft) from the leading end of the cable AND onto the supply spool. Step 2: Pull the cable along the designated pathway to its destination without exceeding tension or bend-radius limits. Step 3: Transfer the ID label from the supply spool to the trailing end of the cable (~600 mm / 2 ft from the cut point). Step 4: Cut the cable free from the supply spool.

clips.label: Question 129
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Rack Assembly and Population Sequence per AVIXA F502.01. Place the shop rack-population and assembly steps in the safest, standards-compliant sequence per AVIXA F502.01. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Lay the rack horizontally on its back over a padded blanket on the shop floor and verify rail squareness. Step 2: Install the heaviest equipment (UPS units and power amplifiers) in the bottom third of the rack, supporting deep chassis on rear rails. Step 3: Mount user-operated media/control gear at ergonomic eye/reach height, high-heat gear near the top, and RF receivers with front-mounted antennas, starting all rack screws by hand. Step 4: Install blanking/vent panels in all unused RU spaces to control airflow and bond the rack chassis and doors to the single technical ground stud.

The differential receiver inverts the polarity, summing audio and cancelling induced noise. Option B. The outer conductive braided shield absorbs all magnetic fields and dissipates them as ground heat. Option C. The twisted conductors filter electromagnetic noise by acting as a passive low-pass capacitor network. Option D. The audio signal voltage drives an internal transformer core to saturate induced radio interference.

clips.label: Question 146
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Loudspeaker Impedance Meter Verification Sequence. Arrange the steps for verifying a distributed loudspeaker circuit with an AC impedance meter (`Z`-meter) in the correct order. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Disconnect the loudspeaker circuit completely from the power amplifier output terminals and calculate the expected total impedance (ZT). Step 2: Select the appropriate ohm range on the AC impedance meter and calibrate the meter to that scale. Step 3: Connect the impedance meter leads to the disconnected speaker line and read the measured AC impedance. Step 4: Verify the reading is within ±10% of the calculated impedance (troubleshooting any low-Z shorts or high-Z opens) before connecting the line to the amplifier.

clips.label: Question 154
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Manual Wall-Mounted Projection Screen Installation Sequence. Order the steps for installing a manual wall-mounted projection screen in the proper sequence. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Verify the mounting location and structural backing, confirming the lowered screen will not block alarms, thermostats, switches, or outlets. Step 2: Measure between the casing suspension points, mark the screen centerline on the wall, and add the case-to-screen offset to the desired top-of-image height. Step 3: Drill and anchor the first end of the screen case at the calculated height. Step 4: Level the screen case horizontally with a spirit level, anchor the second end, and test smooth extension and retraction.

clips.label: Question 162
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Coaxial BNC Cable Stripping and Linear Compression Termination Sequence. Place the steps for terminating a 75-ohm coaxial video cable with a linear-compression BNC connector in the proper sequence. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Slide any required boot/label sleeve onto the cable and calibrate a 3-blade rotary coaxial stripping cassette for the exact cable and BNC model. Step 2: Rotate the 3-blade stripper around the cable end to cut the outer jacket, braided shield, and dielectric to exact stepped lengths without nicking the center conductor. Step 3: Fold back the braided shield as specified and push the prepared cable fully into the linear-compression BNC connector until the center pin seats properly. Step 4: Squeeze the connector axially with the calibrated linear compression hand tool, apply the permanent AVIXA F501.01 label 25–300 mm from the connector, and verify continuity.

Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Powering ON Step 1: Turn on all audio source devices, mixers, DSPs, and crossovers first. Step 2: Powering ON Step 2: Turn on the power amplifiers LAST. Step 3: Powering OFF Step 1: Turn off the power amplifiers FIRST. Step 4: Powering OFF Step 2: Wait 15 seconds for amplifier rails to discharge/mute, then turn off upstream DSPs, mixers, and sources.

clips.label: Question 178
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: EDID Handshake Sequence Between Source and Sink. Order the phases of the digital video EDID handshake between a video Source and a video Sink (display) in chronological sequence. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: The Source sends a +5V Hot Plug signal to the Sink, and the Sink returns the Hot Plug Detect (HPD) signal confirming it is powered and connected. Step 2: The Source requests the Sink's EDID capabilities over the Display Data Channel (DDC). Step 3: The Sink transmits its EDID table (and extension blocks for audio/lip-sync) back to the Source over the DDC. Step 4: The Source configures its output and transmits the video/audio stream matching the Sink's preferred native resolution, refresh rate, and color space.

clips.label: Question 183
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: System Optimization Audio Gain Calibration Sequence (400 Hz + Piezo). Arrange the steps for setting electronic audio gain structure using the System Optimization method (`400 Hz` sine wave + piezo tweeter) in the proper order. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Turn power amplifiers OFF, neutralize all EQs/dynamics, inject a 400 Hz sine wave at 0 dBu into a mixer input, and connect a piezo tweeter (2–20 kHz) to the mixer output. Step 2: Raise the mixer master output until the piezo tweeter buzzes (clipping harmonics), then back off slightly until the piezo goes silent. Step 3: Move the piezo tweeter sequentially to each downstream processor's output up to the amplifier input, driving each stage to the onset of piezo buzz and backing off until silent. Step 4: Return to the mixer and reduce the mixer master output back down to its normal 0 (unity) operating position before calibrating mic trims and power amplifier input attenuators.

clips.label: Question 192
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Camera Zoom Focus and Mechanical Back-Focus Alignment Sequence. Arrange the steps for calibrating a zoom camera's main focus and mechanical back-focus (flange focal distance) in the proper order so the image stays sharp across the entire zoom range. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Place a high-contrast focus chart at the subject position and open the lens iris (reducing light if needed) to narrow depth of field. Step 2: Zoom the lens all the way IN (tight telephoto) on the focus chart and adjust the normal main focus control until crisp. Step 3: Zoom the lens all the way OUT (wide angle) and adjust the mechanical back-focus ring on the lens body until the chart is sharp. Step 4: Repeat the zoom-in (main focus) and zoom-out (back-focus) cycle iteratively until the image stays sharp across the full zoom range, then lock the back-focus ring.

clips.label: Question 199
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Capacitive Reactance (XC) High-Frequency Attenuation in Long Cables. As signal frequency increases, how does capacitive reactance behave between cable conductors, and what effect occurs on long runs? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Capacitive reactance increases linearly, creating high-frequency inductive peaking and standing waves at cable terminations. Option B. Capacitive reactance stabilizes at characteristic cable impedance, inducing low-frequency ground hum across balanced lines. Option C. Capacitive reactance drops to zero at resonance, causing digital packet reflections and clock jitter across serial data streams. Option D. Capacitive reactance decreases, shunting high-frequency signal energy between parallel conductors.

clips.label: Question 205
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Interpreting High versus Low Impedance Meter Readings on Speaker Lines. When testing a disconnected 70V loudspeaker line with an impedance meter, why is a reading far lower than calculated especially dangerous? Choose the best destination for the match. Option A. Lower impedance causes high-voltage flyback spikes that puncture speaker transformer primary winding insulation. Option B. Lower impedance shifts the audio bandwidth, causing severe high-frequency roll-off across distributed ceiling speakers. Option C. Lower impedance forces the amplifier output stage into DC saturation, tripping upstream ground-fault circuit interrupters. Option D. Lower impedance draws excessive current, risking severe amplifier overload and output failure.

clips.label: Question 205, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Lower impedance causes high-voltage flyback spikes that puncture speaker transformer primary winding insulation. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "Lower impedance causes high-voltage flyback…winding insulation" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Decisive rule: By Ohm's law (I = V/Z), a much lower impedance than expected draws dangerously high current that overloads and burns out the amplifier, whereas a higher reading indicates an open branch or under-tapped transformer. Best answer: Lower impedance draws excessive current, risking severe amplifier overload and output failure.

A 16-zone checkerboard pattern measured from five defined viewer locations under ambient lighting.

Contrast ratio is 20:1; a system 'Partially Conforms' if 1 to 4 locations fall below the minimum ratio by no more than 10%. Option C. 18:1 contrast ratio, failing because minimum white luminance must exceed 300 nits under ambient light. Option D. 28:1 contrast ratio, exceeding threshold after subtracting ambient room illuminance from black levels.

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Neutralizing Dynamic Processors Before Setting Gain Structure. Before injecting test tones to establish audio gain structure, how must equalizers and dynamics processors be configured? Choose one labeled answer area. Option A. Power amps at unity, EQs notched at room modes, limiters engaged at 0 dBu, and downward expanders calibrated to speech levels.

Unity Gain equalizes speaker crossover slopes; System Optimization minimizes intermodulation distortion across digital signal processor converters.

clips.label: Question 220
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Power Amplifier Input Attenuator Calibration and Hiss Prevention. What is the function of power amplifier front-panel input attenuators, and what symptom occurs if they are set fully open? Choose the single best answer. Option A. They regulate maximum output wattage; setting them fully open forces output transformers into continuous magnetic saturation and distortion. Option B. They calibrate speaker load impedance; setting them fully open reduces output damping factor, causing muddy low-frequency transient response. Option C. They adjust internal feedback loops; setting them fully open induces high-frequency oscillation and triggers thermal protection shutdown circuits. Option D. They attenuate input voltage; setting them fully open amplifies upstream noise, causing audible hiss.

clips.label: Question 223
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: RTA Cut-Only Equalization Rule and 6 dB Maximum Cut Limit. When equalizing a sound reinforcement system with an RTA, why should an installer use cut-only filters and limit cuts to 6 dB? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Boosting exhausts headroom, while response notches deeper than 6 dB are acoustic cancellations unfixable by EQ. Option B. Boosting shifts crossover phase relationships, while cuts exceeding 6 dB cause passive loudspeaker crossover components to overheat. Option C. Boosting introduces common-mode electrical hum, while cuts exceeding 6 dB reduce microphone preamplifier signal-to-noise ratio below speech thresholds. Option D. Boosting triggers power amplifier thermal limiters, while cuts exceeding 6 dB destabilize DSP finite impulse response filter coefficients.

Ignore deep cancellation notches and read true speaker response 3 dB to 6 dB below constructive peaks.

Switch the video signal format from progressive to interlaced to reduce sensor charge integration time.

segments.text: Choose the single best answer.

segments.label: Option A
segments.text: Option A. Control physical room lighting by shading windows and adding high-CRI front light on the presenter.

segments.label: Option B
segments.text: Option B. Increase electronic shutter speed to 1/2000 second to compress overall optical sensor dynamic range.

segments.label: Option C
segments.text: Option C. Set camera gamma curves to linear and increase master pedestal gain until shadow noise disappears.

segments.label: Option D
segments.text: Option D. Switch the video signal format from progressive to interlaced to reduce sensor charge integration time.

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Projector Mechanical Alignment and Optical Lens Shift versus Electronic Keystone. Why should an installer prioritize mechanical alignment and optical lens shift over electronic keystone correction? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Electronic keystone reduces lamp lifespan by overdriving internal color wheel synchronization timing. Option B. Electronic keystone compresses scan lines and discards native pixels, degrading image resolution. Option C. Electronic keystone shifts projected color temperature toward green, requiring heavy optical filtration. Option D. Electronic keystone introduces severe optical chromatic aberration and barrel distortion across display edges.

clips.label: Question 233, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. 5 ms. Incorrect. Not this one: "5 ms" uses the wrong value, unit, or relationship for the stated quantities. Decisive rule: Because electrical signals travel near the speed of light while acoustic waves travel at 343 m/s (~2.9 ms per meter), a speaker 17.15 m downrange requires 17.15 ÷ 343 = 0.050 s (50 ms) of DSP delay. Best answer: 50 ms.

clips.label: Question 236
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Loudspeaker Polarity Verification (`AP-108` Pulse Tester and Battery Test). Why must loudspeaker polarity be verified across all cabinets, and how does a DC battery touch confirm positive polarity? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Opposite polarity burns voice coils; positive DC voltage pulls the woofer cone inward toward magnet. Option B. Opposite polarity reduces impedance; positive DC voltage stabilizes the crossover network capacitance. Option C. Opposite polarity distorts high frequencies; positive DC voltage centers the voice coil in the magnetic gap. Option D. An out-of-phase speaker cancels low-frequency bass energy from adjacent speakers; an acoustic polarity pulse detector reads '+'.

A digital base station streams uncompressed audio over localized Wi-Fi; verify network latency and packet buffer jitter.

clips.label: Question 262, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Power on amplifiers first, followed by line mixers, and disconnect balanced audio inputs last. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "Power on amplifiers first, followed by line…audio inputs last" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Decisive rule: Whenever powering audio racks manually, staff must turn amplifiers ON last and turn amplifiers OFF first (waiting 15 seconds before shutting down upstream electronics) to prevent speaker-destroying transient thumps. Best answer: Power on DSPs and mixers first, power amps last; reverse sequence when shutting down.

clips.label: Question 264
clips.text: Exam area E. Topic: Organizing Equipment Manuals in the Closeout Package (`DOC-117`). What is best practice for organizing manufacturer equipment manuals in closeout documentation binders? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Bind manuals chronologically by product manufacture date, and retain all copies at integrator headquarters. Option B. Arrange manuals alphabetically by function, and leave a copy with the rack. Option C. Sort documentation by equipment retail price, and deliver copies to client purchasing archives. Option D. File manuals by physical chassis rack unit size, and store them in client corporate legal files.

clips.label: Question 265
clips.text: Exam area E. Topic: Backing Up DSP Configurations and Control Source/Compiled Code. Why must closeout documentation include off-site backups of DSP files, control code, and IP inventories? Choose the single best answer. Option A. To allow rapid system restoration if hardware fails, without re-engineering from scratch. Option B. To satisfy local building department requirements for low-voltage software copyright registration. Option C. To allow casual presenters to modify audio equalization curves directly from conference room laptops. Option D. To synchronize cloud diagnostic profiles automatically during scheduled network firmware updates.

Register, activate, and formally transfer all manufacturer and system warranties to the client.

Connect an optical time-domain reflectometer to measure acoustic echo reflections along copper conductors.

clips.text: Exam area F. Topic: Diagnosing Backward-Wired 70V Loudspeaker Step-Down Transformer. Replacing a ceiling speaker on a 70V line trips the amplifier over-current protection. An impedance sweep reads near zero. What caused this? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Selecting a two-and-a-half watt transformer tap instead of the specified five-watt tap. Option B. Using unshielded twisted-pair cabling instead of plenum-rated coaxial speaker wire. Option C. Reversing speaker polarity on an adjacent ceiling loudspeaker within the same audio zone. Option D. Wiring the step-down transformer backward or connecting an eight-ohm voice coil directly.

clips.label: Question 300, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Selecting a two-and-a-half watt transformer tap instead of the specified five-watt tap. Incorrect. Decisive rule: Connecting an 8-ohm voice coil directly to a 70V line - or wiring a step-down transformer backward so its low-Z secondary faces the amplifier - presents a near-dead short on the constant-voltage line and trips the amplifier. Best answer: Wiring the step-down transformer backward or connecting an eight-ohm voice coil directly.

segments.text: A client requests additional microphones and programming during final acceptance sign-off. How should the installer respond?

segments.label: Response instruction
segments.text: Choose the single best answer.

segments.label: Option A
segments.text: Option A. Refuse to complete the walkthrough and immediately remove the installed equipment from the premises.

segments.label: Option B
segments.text: Option B. Obtain sign-off on the contracted scope and document new requests as a separate change order.

segments.label: Option C
segments.text: Option C. Perform the additional programming on site and supply the extra wireless microphones without additional billing.

segments.label: Option D
segments.text: Option D. Sign the client acceptance document on behalf of the project manager and invoice the original contract balance.

The best answer is: Ground loops circulate current along shields; cutting ground pins creates a lethal shock hazard. **Ground Loop (50/60 Hz hum)** = two devices tied to different AC ground potentials connected by a grounded signal shield. **Fix**: use an audio isolation transformer or common technical ground - **NEVER lift or cut the AC third-prong safety ground!** The source citation remains visible on screen for independent review.
